# Resilience and Self-Recovery Audit — RCJ 2026 IITA Salta

**Date:** 2026-05-18  
**Branch/audited commit:** `feature/initialize-testing-log` @ `c42e535`  
**Method:** 4 independent auditors in parallel (firmware-Teensy, RPi-vision, comms-serial, architecture-FMEA) orchestrated by the skill `rcj-rescue-reviewer`. Director's request: EXCLUSIVE focus on reliability and self-recovery (not performance).

---

## Verdict

> **System self-recovery TODAY: 2/10.** The robot does NOT recover from almost any common failure autonomously. Most leave it **out of control** (active motors, off track) or **dead silent**, with no possibility of intervention (the robot cannot be touched during the run).

With the "minimum resilience architecture" (3 levers, ~half a day's work) it rises to **~6/10**. With the health + degradation layer, **8/10**.

## Decided Objective (Gustavo, 2026-05-18)

**Objective for Incheon = solid and validated 8/10. The 8→10 stretch is post-world championship.** Reason: brutal diminishing returns (2→6 half a day, 6→8 ~1 week, 8→10 weeks); each extra layer is new code that touches validated systems (regression risk); the 8→10 is mainly *validation* (bench time needed to score); and 8→10 does not pass the filter of the regime's own phases. **An 8/10 tested robot wins more runs than a theoretical 10/10 without validation.** Complete decision in `journal/decisions/2026-05-18-objective-reliability-8-incheon.md`. Work plan by sprints in **#114**.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No serial heartbeat + no failsafe | Loose USB-serial cable / Python crash → Teensy repeats last `speed/steer` forever | ❌ NO — out of control, off track | #53 |
| 2 | No HW Watchdog on Teensy | Any SW hang leaves motors active | ❌ NO — only physical switch | #27 |
| 3 | No auto-restart of Main.py | Python process dies (≥4 paths) → Pi blind | ❌ NO — no systemd in the repo | #108 |

| 4b | get_color/colorDataReady without timeout | I2C hung → Teensy frozen | ❌ NO — timeout reverted | #61 |
| 4c | runAngle without timeout or serial drain | Noisy IMU → spins infinitely; serial kill-switch ignored | ❌ NO — never had a fix | #112 |
| 5 | BNO055 without runtime failure detection | I2C hit/noise → navigates with garbage heading unknowingly | ❌ NO — `resetear_bno()` never called on its own | #109 |
| 6 | Reset Teensy (brown-out) without resync | Stalls 4 motors → reset → RPi/Teensy states permanently out of sync | ❌ NO | #72 |
| 7 | `cx_black` uninitialized | Green without black line below (normal scenario) → 100% reproducible crash | ❌ NO — kills the process | #110 |
| 8 | infer_thread without try/except | TFLite failure → thread dies → robot in infinite search | ❌ NO — no respawn | #111 |

## The 3 most dangerous failure cascades

1. **Loose UART cable → total loss of control** (most likely). Vibration loosens the connector → Teensy repeats last command → robot off track. **Instantaneous, without detection.**
2. **APDS9960 hangs I2C → robot frozen silently** (4-5 s). `get_color()` without timeout blocks all firmware; without LED/buzzer (also reverted) there is no diagnosis.
3. **Motor brown-out → permanent desynchronization**. Reset Teensy → RPi/Teensy states out of sync → inert robot without diagnosis until manual intervention = lost round.

## Minimum resilience architecture that is missing (3 levers of maximum impact)

Consensus of the 4 auditors. ~half a day → rises from 2/10 to ~6/10:

1. **UART Heartbeat + safe-state 500ms on Teensy** (#53) → eliminates cascade #1 (most likely).
2. **Restore reverted timeouts #60/#61 + add #112 (runAngle) + HW WDT #27** → eliminates infinite hangs.
3. **systemd `Restart=always` for Main.py + global try/except** (#108) → Pi crash goes from catastrophic to recoverable in ~2s.

Layers that the system DOES NOT have and should have:
- **Layer 1 — HW Watchdog** (Teensy, `WDT_T4`, callback that stops motors).
- **Layer 2 — Health table of subsystems** (`bno_ok`, `apds_ok`, `tof_ok`, `encoder_stall` → safe degraded decisions).
- **Layer 3 — Explicit safe-state** (motors 0, wait for recovery, escape from rescue FSM by timeout).
